scores.answer:
The checkable numeric forecasts match the formal guidance. Fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of $2.05 to $2.25 matches the formal range [1][2]. Fourth-quarter revenue of $9.7 billion to $10.5 billion also matches [1][2]. The third-quarter guidance reported by Motley Fool, $9.2 billion to $10.0 billion in revenue and $2.10 to $2.30 in adjusted EPS, matches the formal guidance [3][4]. Several directional statements have no formal numeric guidance to compare against, so they cannot be judged. Qualcomm said revenue from its Apple modem business would decline faster than previously expected, with the decline starting in the fiscal fourth quarter (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [5]. It also said non-handset growth would offset the Apple reduction over time (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [5]. It expects top-line growth in fiscal 2027 (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [6]. It plans price increases beginning September 1 (reported by finance.yahoo.com, theverge.com) [5][7]. None of these has a formal figure to compare against (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [5][6]. One claim, that fourth-quarter adjusted earnings would fall below Wall Street expectations, was reviewed as wrong and left out of the outcome counts (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [5]. The fourth-quarter GAAP EPS guidance of $1.22 to $1.42 is still pending [2].
Left out because they could not be verified (cited only from news, not supported by the cited evidence): 3 statements.

scores.answer:
Meta's executives made no stored management statements about 2025 capex that I could find. Guidance was raised over the year: the January release gave $60-65 billion [1], the April release $64-72 billion [2], the July release $66-72 billion [3], and the October release $70-72 billion, including principal payments on finance leases [4]. Each of those ranges was reported as beaten against the first-reported actual of $72.2 billion [1][2][3][4]. The latest 10-K reports FY2025 capex of $69,691M [5], which is below the final $70-72 billion range [4][5]. The guidance rows note the basis was not stated and that the comparison used the GAAP actual [4].

scores.question: In May 2024, what did Nvidia say it expected for revenue in the following quarter, as reported in the news, and how did the result compare?
failure_details: 0 numbers_cited: a sentence with a number has no citation: In May 2024, Nvidia said it expected second-quarter fiscal 2025 revenue of about $28 billion, plus or minus 2%.
scores.answer:
In May 2024, Nvidia said it expected second-quarter fiscal 2025 revenue of about $28 billion, plus or minus 2% (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [1][2]. The formal guidance was issued May 22, 2024, in the earnings release [3]. Reports also described it as up 107% year over year (reported by fool.com) [4].
The result beat that outlook. First-reported revenue was $30.04 billion, $2.04 billion (7.3%) above the $28.0 billion point estimate [3]. Fool.com reported that Wall Street had modeled $26.66 billion for the quarter, but that analyst figure is not a company statement (reported by fool.com) [5].

Nvidia guided fiscal Q2 2027 revenue to $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, in its May 20, 2026 earnings release, not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China [1]. scores.question: What did Apple's executives say about how fast iPhone Duo shipments will grow next year?
notes: does not say management made no such claim

scores.answer:
I could not find any Apple executive statement about how fast iPhone Duo shipments will grow next year. The only revenue outlook I found is a September-quarter growth range of 9% to 11% (reported by 247wallst.com, tikr.com) [1][2]. It appears only in news reports. Yahoo Finance reported it as $111.7 billion to $113.7 billion (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [3]. Apple's stored earnings releases contain no revenue guidance [4], so I cannot confirm the range from a filing or guidance row. On Duo itself, the news describes demand and delivery timing, not a growth forecast. Motley Fool reported that preorders sold out quickly, stretching delivery estimates into January [5]. It also reported that delivery dates moved from Oct. 23 into late January (reported by fool.com) [6]. CBS News reported the device is backordered until 2027 [7]. Bloomberg headlined that Duo orders slipped into 2027 [8]. 9to5Mac's headline says Apple called pre-order demand "extraordinary" [9], but I only have the headline, not the full remarks. The Motley Fool and 9to5Mac items do not name a speaker, so I cannot attribute them to a specific executive.
Left out because they could not be verified (not supported by the cited evidence): one statement.
